Original Chinese:
床前明月光 (chuáng qián míng yuè guāng)
疑是地上霜 (yí shì dì shàng shuāng)
举头望明月 (jǔ tóu wàng míng yuè)
低头思故乡 (dī tóu sī gù xiāng)

Step 1: Chinese to English

床前明月光
- 床 (chuáng) = bed/couch
- 前 (qián) = in front of
- 明 (míng) = bright
- 月 (yuè) = moon
- 光 (guāng) = light

"Before my bed, bright moonlight" - I could say "Bright moonlight before my bed" but the original has a subject-verb structure. "Bright moonlight shines before my bed" captures the imagery of the light being present.

疑是地上霜
- 疑 (yí) = to suspect/doubt/think
- 是 (shì) = is
- 地上 (dì shàng) = on the ground
- 霜 (shuāng) = frost

"I suspect it is frost on the ground" or "I think it is frost on the ground" - "suspect" captures the uncertainty better, as the poet is momentarily confused by the bright light.

举头望明月
- 举 (jǔ) = raise/lift
- 头 (tóu) = head
- 望 (wàng) = gaze/look


- 明月 (míng yuè) = bright moon
- 月 (yuè) = moon

"Lifting my head, I gaze at the bright moon" - this captures the action and the object of contemplation.

低头思故乡
- 低 (dī) = lower
- 头 (tóu) = head
- 思 (sī) = think/miss
- 故乡 (gù xiāng) = hometown/home
